Industry · Healthcare & Life Sciences Know Which Models Touch a Clinical Decision.

Clinical AI rarely arrives through procurement. It arrives because a tool helps, and becomes relied upon before anyone reviews it. Who signed off the one your team uses every day?

02

Three Gaps in Clinical Systems

I

The Tool Entered Through Clinical Enthusiasm, Not Procurement.

Triage support and imaging pre-reads usually arrive because a clinician found something that genuinely helps. The intent is good. Has any committee reviewed it as a clinical system since?

II

Accountability Gets Assigned Retrospectively Unless It Is Assigned Now.

The question of who is answerable for a recommendation is rarely settled while the tool is working well. Consider which of your pathways would struggle to answer it under pressure.

III

Shadow AI Is Already in the Pathway.

Documentation tools and decision support enter through departmental budgets, outside formal approval. Ask your clinical leads what is in daily use and compare the list to your governance register.

04

Common Questions

What does an AI governance gap assessment cover in a clinical setting?

Which tools influence a clinical decision, who approved each one, how patient data reaches them, and whether clinicians can demonstrably reject the output.

Does the UAE PDPL apply to patient data held by a private clinic?

Yes, and it applies extraterritorially wherever the personal data of UAE residents is processed.

How do we evidence that a clinician can override a recommendation?

Through interface evidence and override rates from real use, which is the part most deployments never capture.

Do you assess software as a medical device?

We assess how the software is governed, used and overridden in your pathways. Classification as a medical device rests with your regulatory affairs team and the device regulator, and we flag any classification question at scoping.

Can you assess one clinical pathway rather than the whole hospital group?

Yes — pathway by pathway is slower but produces something a clinical governance committee can actually act on.
